slate.name: symindex
merged_from: tagswitch part (3) for the remaining pass (optional)
slate.rationale: Largest single profile share that has an exact fix. Program.initializeStandardLibraryCaches is 13.7% inclusive in allon.txt, 16.7% in the gdb sampling and about 13-14% in ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10. It makes 24 full scans of stdlib syntax, one per StandardLibraryEntity, and each scan does an `as? any Annotatable` existential cast on every node. Most of the 7% conformance-cache self time comes from these casts. The fix is one pass that builds an inverted index. It is pure code motion with a trivial equivalence argument.
slate.spec:
Flag: `symindex` in TyperExperiments (Sources/FrontEnd/Typer/TyperCounters.swift).
Where: Sources/FrontEnd/Program.swift:2004-2018 initializeStandardLibraryCaches. It is called from Typer.swift:40-42 on every stdlib typing and from Program.swift:2075-2077 when the stdlib is loaded from an archive. Related code: select(from:_:) at 2102-2106, SyntaxFilter .symbol at 2141-2142, symbol(annotating:) at 1458-1462, annotations/annotation at 1651-1662.
Change: under the flag, build `var table: [String: [AnySyntaxIdentity]] = [:]` with one loop over `modules.values[a].syntax`, in the same order that select(from:) uses. For each node n with `let s = symbol(annotating: n)`, append n to table[s]. Then, for each `e in StandardLibraryEntity.allCases`, in the same order as today, set `let b = table[e.rawValue]?.uniqueElement` and keep the existing body: castToDeclaration, the precondition/allowPartialStandardLibrary handling, and the assignment to standardLibraryDeclarations[e]. The old loop stays in the else branch.
Optional micro-step: skip nodes whose SyntaxTag is not a declaration before the `as? any Annotatable` cast. Only do this if every Annotatable conformer is a declaration; check this with grep for `: Annotatable` / `Annotatable,` conformances. Otherwise precompute a per-SyntaxTag bit (`tag.value is any Annotatable.Type`, evaluated once per tag) and test that bit instead of casting.
Soundness: filter preserves order and the predicate is identical, so table[s] equals select(from: a, .symbol(s)) element for element, and uniqueElement gives the same value, including nil when the symbol is missing or duplicated. The function has no other side effects. The precomputed tag bit is exact because conformance of a struct type to a protocol is fixed at compile time.
Test: semtest/dump with only symindex, and with all flags, over the 192 tests, the stdlib and the workloads: they must be byte-identical. Add a debug assertion, run once, that the old and new maps are equal. Benchmark type.stdlib.
slate.expected_gain: stdlib typing about -13% (13.7% x 23/24, about 20 ms of 160 ms). It saves the same absolute time in every compilation that types or loads the stdlib, so ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10 also gain about -13% of the whole run, and breadth80 and members-big gain the same 20 ms.

slate.name: typevec
slate.rationale: The type store is the hottest piece of infrastructure. StableSet.subscript.getter is 12.6% inclusive on the stdlib and 13.9% on breadth80. StableDictionary.assignValue is 3.6% on the stdlib and 11.9% on breadth80. TypeStore.demand is 11.4%, and the TupleCache/getTupleTypeMetadata2 traffic is about 3.4%. The disassembly shows the cause: StableCollections is a separate module and is neither inlinable nor specialized, so every projection runs unspecialized generic code. Within TypeStore, the same flag also removes the 4 dynamic casts and the box in demand, the Optional and tuple metadata in TypeTree.equals, and the 2 alias-probe casts per unification step. All of these are local constant-factor changes with the same soundness argument (identical identities), so one flag keeps the matrix small. I checked the claims against the code. `types` is private (TypeStore.swift:22), and its only mutation is insert at :93 through StableSet.insert, i.e. assignValue (StableSet.swift:71-73); nothing calls remove. TypeAlias.properties is `.hasAliases` (TypeAlias.swift:20-22). The alias probes are at TypeStore.swift:998-1002, before the `unify` dispatch.
slate.spec:
Flag: `typevec`, read once into a stored `let fast: Bool` in TypeStore.init. Do not read the global var in hot paths.
File Sources/FrontEnd/Types/TypeStore.swift.
(A) Storage. Add `private var trees: ContiguousArray<AnyTypeTree> = []`, `private var tags: [UInt8] = []` and `private var index: [AnyTypeTree: Int] = [:]`. Keep `types` for the off path. In insert(_:) (:92-98), when fast: look up `index[k]`; if it is present, return `.init(offset: i, properties: t.properties)`; otherwise set i = trees.count, append to trees and tags, and set index[k] = i. Prefer a single probe through the `index[k, default: trees.count]` modify accessor. The tag is the dense index of TypeTag(type(of: t)), from TypeTag.indices or a new static table [ObjectIdentifier: UInt8] built once. underestimatedCount and reserveCapacity forward to trees and index. In subscript(n: AnyTypeIdentity) (:733-746), the default branch returns `fast ? trees[n.offset].wrapped : types[n.offset].wrapped`.
(B) Tag fast paths. Add `func tagIndex(_ n: AnyTypeIdentity) -> UInt8?`, which returns nil for the predefined identities (.error, .void, .never) and for variables, and tags[n.offset] otherwise. Use it in tag(of:) (:106-109), cast/castUnchecked (:477-489; a mismatching tag returns nil without projecting), isParameter/hasContext (:111-127), and head, contextAndHead and open (:177-232): if the tag is neither UniversalType nor Implication, return directly, as the `default:` arm does.
(C) Interning, ex-internfast. In demand<T: TypeTree>(_:) (:71-73), branch on `T.self == ErrorType.self`, `Tuple.self`, `UniversalType.self` and `TypeVariable.self`; these comparisons fold at specialization. Use `as!` only inside the matching branch, keep the same `where` conditions (u == .empty, isNever(u)), and otherwise call a generic `insert<U: TypeTree>(_ t: U)` so that the value is boxed once, into AnyTypeTree. In demand(any:) (:76-89), compare `type(of: t)` with those metatypes instead of running the `switch` of `is`/`as` casts. In Sources/FrontEnd/Types/TypeTree.swift:28-30, implement equals(_:) as `guard type(of: other) == Self.self, let o = other as? Self else { return false }; return self == o` under the flag. Put the flag in a `static let` that equals reads.
(D) Alias probes, ex-tagswitch(1). In unifiable at TypeStore.swift:998-1002, guard each probe as `else if (!fast || a[.hasAliases]), let t = self[a] as? TypeAlias` and likewise for b. dealiased (:830-844) already uses the same guard.
Soundness: (A) A StableSet that never sees a remove has no tombstones, so a new key gets position == count, and an existing key is found by the same Hashable/== relation that the Swift Dictionary uses. Every AnyTypeIdentity, offsets included, is therefore bit-identical to the baseline, and so is everything downstream. (B) tags[i] is written once from the dynamic type of the stored tree. All type trees are structs, so a tag comparison is equivalent to a successful `as?`. (C) There are no subclasses, so `x is S` holds iff type(of: x) == S.self. When the dynamic types differ, `other as? Self` is nil and the old `self == nil` is false, the same as the early return. (D) Every TypeAlias identity carries .hasAliases, because the identity stores t.properties. Predefined identities and variables are never aliases, so a probe skipped when the bit is clear would have failed.
Risk notes: copying the Program value (solver forks copy Typer) now retains 3 buffers instead of 1, and copy-on-write on the first insertion after a fork copies the arrays. The baseline already copies the StableSet in that case, but measure breadth80 and ovl. Do not change StableCollections.
Test: dump identical with typevec alone and with all flags, across the corpus, the stdlib and the workloads. Add a debug mode that runs both stores side by side and asserts equal offsets on every insert for the stdlib run.
slate.expected_gain: stdlib typing about -15 to -18%: projection about -10%, interning metadata and casts about -3 to -4%, alias probes and context/head casts about -1.5%. breadth80 about -18 to -22% of the run. members-big about -4 to -5%. ovl and ovr get the stdlib share.

slate.name: givenfacts
slate.rationale: canDeriveCoercions is 12.6% inclusive on the stdlib (allon.txt) and canDeriveCoercion(_:applying:) 9.6%. 8% of it runs under anonymousImplementation, where the stack is non-empty and both the index and the memo writes are disabled (Typer.swift:4268-4285 and 4303-4305). The exact counts show 58,400 canDeriveCoercion calls, 37,488 misses and only 10,170 distinct keys. The stdlib declares no coercion source at all: every given in StandardLibrary is a conformance (`T is P` or `<..> => X is P`). So the scan almost always concludes 'false' after calling declaredType and contextAndHead on every visible given. A given whose declared type is settled has a fixed classification. That makes it possible to skip non-sources in O(1), to write the per-(given, pair) memo under any stack, and to answer 'no sources visible' without a scan. It is exact and needs no index. This is the lazy, stack-safe form of dtree part (a) and of coesrc.
slate.spec:
Flag: `givenfacts`.
Files: Sources/FrontEnd/Typer/Typer.swift. canDeriveCoercions 4246-4290; canDeriveCoercion(_:applying:) 4298-4337; declaredType(of: Given) 1650-1699; expression(referringTo:) 4180-4194; givens(visibleFrom:) 4130-4154; notOnStack 5272-5281; Memos 52-150.
Data: `struct GivenFacts { kind: Kind; context: ContextClause; head: AnyTypeIdentity }` with `enum Kind { case none, wildcard, equality(EqualityWitness.ID) }`. Add Memos fields `givenFacts: [Given: GivenFacts]`, `scopeToSources: [ScopeIdentity: [Given]]` (set only once every given visible from the scope is settled) and, optionally, `givenWitness: [Given: WitnessExpression]`.
settled(g): `.user(d)` is settled iff d's type is already memoized in the program (the same store setType writes; use the read-only accessor, e.g. program[d.module].type(assignedTo: d) != nil, and NEVER call declaredType to find out). `.nested(_, h)` is settled iff h is settled. The built-in, coercion and recursive cases are always settled. `.assumed` is settled; its type is carried in the environment.
facts(g): return the cached value, or nil if !settled(g). Otherwise compute declaredType(of: g); this has no side effect because g is settled, and for .nested contextOfSelf is memoized and introduce/demand hash-cons to existing ids. Then classify exactly as 4310-4330 does: `u.context.parameters.contains(u.head)` gives wildcard; `cast(u.head, to: EqualityWitness.self)` gives equality; anything else gives none. Store and return.
canDeriveCoercion under the flag: after the existing memo read (4301), `if let f = facts(g)`, switch on f.kind. For .none the result is 0b00. For .wildcard it is 0b11. For .equality, run the existing open/unifiable code with f.context.parameters and the lhs/rhs of the witness. In all three cases write the memo whenever `p.isClosed`, whatever the stack. Otherwise take the old path unchanged, and afterwards call `_ = facts(g)` if g is now settled.
canDeriveCoercions under the flag, after the existing memo read: compute `s = sourcesIfSettled(scopeOfUse)`. This is cached in scopeToSources. Compute it only when every given of the unfiltered visible list is settled: enumerate the groups exactly as givens(visibleFrom:) does but without notOnStack, and keep the givens with kind != none, in order. If s is non-nil, iterate `chain(environment.givens, s.filter(notOnStack))` with the same accumulator, early exit and memo writes as today. If s is empty, environment.givens is empty and p is closed, the result is false and may be memoized even when an implicit is on the stack, because with no source at all the filtered list has none either. If s is nil (something unsettled), run the old loop, which already benefits from the O(1) per-given path.
Optional part (b): expression(referringTo:) returns a cached WitnessExpression for settled givens (4,104 calls for 89 distinct givens).
Counters: givenfacts.fast, givenfacts.unsettled, givenfacts.sourceListHits.
Soundness: (1) Once g is settled, declaredType(g) returns a fixed id: setType is write-once and the other parts are memoized or hash-consed. canDeriveCoercion(p, g) is therefore a pure function of (p, that id), except that the equality branch's open() allocates fresh variables, which only perturbs numbering (index and solver already do this). (2) Skipping the computation for a settled non-source returns the same 0b00, and the declaredType call it omits would have been a no-op. (3) The baseline reads the per-given memo at 4301 under any stack, so writing a value under a stack stores exactly what any later computation would produce. (4) A source list built only when all visible givens are settled, filtered by notOnStack at query time, visits the same sources in the same order as the old loop. The non-sources it omits contribute 0 and have no side effects, and an early exit can only occur at a source. (5) Unsettled givens always go through the baseline code, so the order of first-time declaredType evaluations, and with it cycle-cut behaviour, is unchanged.
Test: semtest identical (alone and with all flags) on the corpus, the stdlib, the workloads, and review/names/*.hylo and review/loopcheck/*.hylo (cyclic programs that exercise unsettled givens). Also check counters: givenfacts.fast should be close to the former miss count (about 37k).
slate.expected_gain: stdlib about -8 to -11%: canDeriveCoercion from 9.6% to under 1%, and the canDeriveCoercions loop plus givens(visibleFrom:) from about 3% to under 1%. breadth80 about -5% (canDeriveCoercions 6.5% there; with no source the scan becomes O(1) once all givens are settled). members-big, ovl and ovr get the stdlib share.

slate.name: nocopy
slate.rationale: About 6% of leaf samples are copies and destroys of a whole Typer or Program value. They come from method partial applications and from the escaping AnyIterator in Program.scopes(from:), and the disassembly confirms this ('outlined init with copy of Typer' inside the loop of lookup(_:memberOfTraitVisibleFrom:); 3 swift_allocObject calls plus a Program copy in scopes(from:); 2 Program copies in hasImplicitOnStack). Verified call sites: Typer.swift:4825 `.filter(resolvableWithQualification(_:))`, 3979 and 4135 `.filter(notOnStack(_:))`, 4758 `allSatisfy(program.isOverloadable(_:))`, 5285 `contains(where: program.isImplicit)`, and scopes(from:) at 2001, 4134 and 4770. All of the predicates are non-mutating (resolvableWithQualification at 4854 and notOnStack at 5272 are `private func`). It is trivially exact.
slate.spec:
Flag: `nocopy`, hoisted into a local `let` in each function.
Typer.swift:
- 4825: `var ms = lookup(name, lexicallyIn: .init(node: d)); if ms.isEmpty { continue }; ms.removeAll(where: { !resolvableWithQualification($0) })`. removeAll keeps order. The non-escaping closure literal borrows self instead of copying it.
- 3979 and 4135: `.filter({ notOnStack($0) })`; at 4135, skip the call entirely when givens(lexicallyIn: s) is empty.
- 4758: `ds.allSatisfy({ program.isOverloadable($0) })`.
- 5285: `declarationsOnStack.contains(where: { program.isImplicit($0) })`.
- 2001, 4134, 4770: replace `for s in program.scopes(from: x)` with `var c: ScopeIdentity? = x; while let s = c { ...body...; c = program.parent(containing: s) }`. Mirror exactly the iteration of Program.swift:1049-1059 (start node included, stop when the parent is nil). Keep any `break`/`return` semantics. Leave Program.scopes(from:) unchanged for its other callers.
Check in the code that each loop body neither mutates the scope tree nor depends on the iterator being a snapshot; scopes are fixed after scoping.
Verification: semtest identical. Optionally, objdump the new binary and check that 'outlined init with copy of Typer' no longer appears in lookup(_:memberOfTraitVisibleFrom:). Counters unchanged.
Soundness: the same predicate is applied to the same elements in the same order. Only the capture mode changes, and the predicates are pure reads during the call. The manual loop visits the same sequence s, parent(s), ... as the AnyIterator.
slate.expected_gain: stdlib about -3 to -4% (Typer copy about 2.1-2.6%, scopes(from:) about 0.7%, hasImplicitOnStack and isOverloadable about 0.5%). members-big about -1.5 to -2%, breadth80 about -2%, ovl and ovr the stdlib share.

slate.name: solver1
slate.rationale: The counters show that `solver` is pure overhead on the stdlib: 338 probes, 0 pruned, 0 commits, goalSteps +12%, refreshScans 63 -> 3052, and all-minus-solver was faster in 3/3 timing rounds. Its only known divergence, positive/overload-priority.hylo, comes from a commit in a system with a single overload. Deferring only when two or more overload sets are pending makes such systems run baseline code verbatim, which removes both the overhead and the divergence. The ovl/ovr wins (8 and 10 simultaneous sets) are kept. Verified in Solver.swift:102 (`let deferring = TyperExperiments.solver`), 104-118 (loop-top handling), 147-151 (unconditional park), 166 (refresh gated by !deferring) and 594-630 (resolveParked/commit).
slate.spec:
Flag: `solver1`, independent of `solver`. If both are on, solver1 wins; document this.
Solver.swift, in solution(betterThanOrEqualTo:using:):
- Replace the constant `deferring` with a computed test `func deferringNow() -> Bool { (TyperExperiments.solver && !TyperExperiments.solver1) || (TyperExperiments.solver1 && (!parked.isEmpty || probing)) }`. Hoist the two flags into lets.
- Loop top (:104-118): `if !deferringNow() { break }`. The rest is as today: probing stops with probeFinished, then resolveParked, then refresh.
- Overload arm (:147-151): `if TyperExperiments.solver1 { if !parked.isEmpty || fresh.contains(where: { me.goals[$0] is OverloadConstraint }) { me.parked.append(g); return .running }; return me.solve(overload: g).map(SolverStatus.terminated(_:)) ?? .canceled }`.
- Line 166: `if fresh.isEmpty && !deferringNow() { refreshCoercionAndWideningConstraints() }`.
- resolveParked (:594-630): under solver1, if parked.count == 1, remove it and `return solve(overload: g, among: k.candidates)...` directly: no probe, no commit (baseline forking).
Counters: solver1.parkedSystems, plus the existing probes/commits.
Soundness: consider a system in which no two overload constraints are ever pending at the same time (pending meaning in fresh or parked when one is popped). There parked stays empty and probing is false, so deferringNow() is false at every check, and the loop executes exactly the baseline statements: an immediate solve(overload:), refresh at 166, and break at the loop top. Forks inherit the same rule. Systems with two or more simultaneous sets behave like `solver`, apart from the last set being forked rather than probed, which is the baseline action for it. solver1 therefore strictly shrinks the divergence surface of `solver`. It does not prove the multi-set case: the pending solver review and the representation issue of the commit path (X vs A<Void>) remain, and the commit should record its choice exactly as solve(overload:) does.
Test: overload-priority.hylo must become dump-identical. stdlib counters: probes about 0, goalSteps back to about 9.5k, refreshScans about 63. ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10 must keep their probes/commits and their roughly 1e4x speedup. Full corpus semtest with solver1 alone and with all flags (solver replaced by solver1).
slate.expected_gain: stdlib about -3 to -6% relative to `solver` on, and about 0% relative to the baseline. ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10 unchanged (about 4 orders of magnitude better than the baseline). Other workloads unchanged. It also removes a known divergence.

slate.name: absfast
slate.rationale: absmodel stays necessary (div-grow needs it, and it removes 36 subgoals and 516 matches on the stdlib), but its build is pure cost where it refutes nothing. On breadth80 the 80-fact buckets are inserted quadratically, with copy-on-write copies (AbstractResolution.swift:223-231 `var bucket = facts[k] ?? []`, a linear subsumes scan, then the write-back), which costs 35-53 ms of about 350-430 ms of user typing. Every user module also rebuilds a model of 63-65 facts from all stdlib givens (Typer.swift:3985-3987, from-scratch branch), which costs 1.4-2.2 ms, about 50% of chain8's user typing. Both fixes keep the set of refutations, or only shrink it, and that is safe because a refutation is only ever of a failing subgoal.
slate.spec:
Flag: `absfast`. It is a no-op unless `absmodel` is on.
(1) AbstractResolution.swift. Read the flag in AbstractResolutionModel.init into a stored Bool. Add `exact: [Key: Set<Term>]` for ground, top-free facts and `general: [Key: [Term]]`, plus a pre-offset copy `generalOffset: [Key: [Term]]` (offsettingVariables(by: 1 << 20) computed once at insertion). insert(_:) (:223-231): if f is ground and top-free, return false when `exact[k]` contains f or some g in general[k] subsumes f. Otherwise, for a non-ground f, run the full subsumes scan over the whole bucket, as today. To append, use `facts[k, default: []].append(f)` (in place), and update exact or general/generalOffset. Keep `facts[k]` in the same order and keep factCount, so that isInconclusive and the factLimit behaviour are unchanged. mayDerive (:117-127): for a ground, top-free query q, return true if exact[k] contains q, otherwise scan generalOffset[k] in order. For any other query, scan as today but use the pre-offset copies.
Prerequisite: the engineer must first check AbstractResolutionModel.subsumes and unify for ground, top-free terms. Confirm that subsumes(g, f) with both ground and top-free is exactly g == f, and that unify(q, f) with both ground and top-free is q == f. If .top or another wildcard symbol behaves otherwise, restrict the fast path accordingly.
(2) Typer.swift abstractModel(visibleFrom:) (3965-4010), from-scratch branch (3985-3987). Under the flag, let `i = imports(of: scopeOfUse.file)`. If some imported module j has `cache.moduleToAbstractModel[j]` with the same depth, set m = that model, firstNew = m.clauses.count, and local = all groups of givens(visibleFrom: scopeOfUse) except the givens(atTopLevelOf: j) group members. Then add the clauses and run saturate(from: firstNew) as today. Each imported module's model is a superset of what the user sees: it was built from j's file scope, which covers all of j's top-level givens. A superset of facts is still a sound over-approximation, so it can only make mayDerive return true more often, never false wrongly.
(3) Outside the flag, in the tc/resolution PR: change the default of TyperExperiments.absDepth (TyperCounters.swift:65-68) from 3 to 2. Without the environment variable, stdlib typing with absmodel takes 14.9 s at k=3 against 0.8 s at k=2, with 224 vs 225 refutations.
Soundness: (1) is bit-identical in model contents and order, so it makes the same refutations. Check that the absmodel.* counters (facts, refuted, inconclusive, work) are identical with and without absfast on all workloads. (2) gives a model whose least-fixpoint denotation ⊇ the from-scratch one (equal when j's top-level givens are exactly the imported group). mayDerive is monotone in the denotation, so refutations ⊆ today's. Every remaining refutation is still of a non-derivable goal, and a refuted subgoal contributes no thread in the baseline either, so the elaboration is unchanged under the same assumption that makes absmodel sound. Test: semtest identical with absmodel,absfast vs baseline and vs absmodel alone.
slate.expected_gain: breadth80 user typing about -8 to -12% (absmodel.micros from 35-53 ms to a few ms). User typing of small programs about -1.5 to -2 ms per module (chain8 about -50%, ovl-8-8 about -15 to -20%, div-* -20 to -40%). stdlib about -0.5 to -1.5%. The absDepth default removes an 18x pitfall.

slate.name: memberskip
slate.rationale: On the stdlib, `names` removes the most work of any flag (with all others on: matches 14079 -> 3541, applies calls 7216 -> 32). memberindex's extension side would make members-big 2.5x faster. Both are UNSOUND as specified. The review's names-1 shows that skipping applies(e, q) also skips its side effects: the first-time evaluation of extendeeType(e) and, in the slow path, summon over the visible givens, which forces declaredType of givens. memberindex inherits this, because its soundness argument says 'justified by the argument accepted for names'. A sound rule: skip a non-declaring extension only when its applies call provably has no observable side effect. That holds when (i) e's extendee type is already memoized, (ii) the rigid nominal heads of e's extendee and q differ, so the match fails at the head, and (iii) the scope applies runs in has no coercion source and all its givens are settled, so the canDeriveCoercions call after the failed head unification returns false without forcing anything. The stdlib declares no coercion source, so (iii) usually holds once its givens are typed. The trait-side index of memberindex is exact as proposed: lookup(name, lexicallyIn: trait) is syntactic, and the baseline skips empty results at 4826.
slate.spec:
Flag: `memberskip`. Independent of `names`: when it is on, it decides; `names` keeps its own behaviour only when memberskip is off.
Part T (exact, trait side). Add a Memos cache `scopeToTraitsByName: [ScopeIdentity: [String: [TraitDeclaration.ID]]]`, built from traits(visibleFrom:) (Typer.swift:5035-5061) in order, keyed by each identifier of declarations(lexicallyIn: trait). In lookup(_:memberOfTraitVisibleFrom:) (4820-4831), iterate only `byName[name.identifier] ?? []` and keep the existing body: lookup + refineLookupResults + the resolvableWithQualification filter, without the partial application (see nocopy).
Part E (extensions). In resolve(_:declaredIn:applyingTo:in:statically:) (4675-4708), after the declarationsOnStack check, and when e does not declare n.identifier (`declarations(lexicallyIn: .init(node: e))[n.identifier] == nil`), skip e iff ALL of the following hold:
 (a) extendeeType(e) is already memoized. Use the memo that the setType at Typer.swift ~1760 writes, read without side effects; never call extendeeType to find out.
 (b) H(e) and H(q) are both defined and differ. H(x) is the declaration identity of the rigid nominal head of x: take contextAndHead(x).head, dealias it, and if it is a TypeApplication take its abstraction. A struct, enum, trait or other nominal declaration type, or a MachineType, is rigid. A generic parameter, variable, associated/remote type, tuple, arrow, metatype, alias or anything else gives undefined. Cache H(e) per extension.
 (c) Let s' be the scope applies(e, q, scopeOfUse) actually runs in: walk parents while givens(lexicallyIn:) is empty, mirroring 4948-4950. Then coercionFree(s') holds: every given visible from s' (unfiltered) is settled and none is a wildcard (`<T> T`) or an equality (`T ~ U`) given. Cache only `true` per scope. Settledness is monotone and the classification is fixed, so true stays true. Share settled()/classification with givenfacts if both land, but implement it so that it works with givenfacts off.
Otherwise call applies as today. Counter memberskip.skipped (compare it with names.skippedExtensions on the same runs) and memberskip.kept.
Part E2 (index, optional second step under the same flag, once E is gated). Per scope, keep the visible-extension list annotated with positions, plus byName[identifier], byHead[H(e)] and a residual list R of extensions with undefined H(e) or an unsettled extendee. Prune R lazily as extendees settle. When coercionFree(s') holds and H(q) is defined, iterate the position-ordered merge of byName[n.identifier], byHead[H(q)] and R, and apply the same per-e test. Otherwise run the plain loop.
Soundness obligation, which the engineer must check in the code before gating: when (a)-(c) hold, applies(e, q, scopeOfUse) evaluates as follows. givens(lexicallyIn:) is syntactic. extendeeType(e) returns the memo. The t == u fast path fails because the heads differ. The cache read has no effect. In the slow path, formThread(matching: w, to: head(q), in: .empty) runs match. Unifying the opened extendee head with head(q) fails at the rigid head, with or without `unify` (TypeStore.swift:1040-1041, unifiableSameShape). The coercion handler records the pair, match calls canDeriveCoercions over the visible givens of s' with an empty environment, and that returns false with no first-time evaluation, because everything is settled and there is no source. The thread dies with .next([]) (Typer.swift ~3776-3781), and takeSummonResults returns nil. So the only effects are memo writes of values that any later computation reproduces, plus fresh-variable and type-store numbering, which the oracle normalizes and which names/index already perturb. Read formThread/match/takeSummonResults line by line to confirm that no other path is taken: for instance the `coerced` slow path, or alias handling on the q side, which must be dealiased before H. Then the skipped call is unobservable, which refutes the names-1 mechanism: n04 is no longer skipped because E2's extendee is unsettled, and n11/n12 are not skipped because the given is unsettled.
Test: semtest with memberskip alone and with all flags (names off) on the corpus, the stdlib, the workloads and review/names/*.hylo (n01-n17, t03). All must be identical to the baseline, including the cases where names diverges. Counters: memberskip.skipped on the stdlib and members-big compared with names.skippedExtensions.
slate.expected_gain: If (c) holds most of the time: on the stdlib, most of names' saving (names removes about 10k matches and the slow applies paths; estimate -10 to -20% of typing, against all-minus-names). members-big: Part E alone gives about -30 to -40% (the cheap test replaces applies, but the scan stays O(#ext)); with E2, about -55 to -65%. Part T: stdlib -1 to -2% beyond nocopy. Measure memberskip.skipped/names.skippedExtensions first: if early-typing unsettledness blocks most skips on the stdlib, the gain shrinks accordingly.

slate.name: membermemo
merged_from: cyclecut taint counter as infrastructure (non-semantic use)
slate.rationale: resolve(memberOf:) is 30% inclusive on the stdlib. gdb shows that 1804 type-qualified calls have only 236-254 distinct (name, q, static/file) keys, so 86% are repeats. The fresh part of each call (nativeMemberOf, the trait scan, qualificationForSelection/reify/typeOfImplementation, fresh) is about 15% of the run. The relaxed mode's soundness argument (memo reads and writes under a non-empty stack) is subtle. Strict mode is simpler: write and read only with an empty declaration stack, write only if no stack-dependent decision or cycle cut occurred during the call, and store no variable-bearing candidate. It keeps a large part of the gain at moderate risk. Ranked last because it is the riskiest member of the slate and its gain shrinks once nocopy, givenfacts and memberskip land.
slate.spec:
Flag: `membermemo`.
Infrastructure: `var stackObservations = 0` in Typer. Increment it (1) in the 4 cycle branches (Typer.swift 1314-1318 Binding, 1353-1357 Conformance, 1558-1562 TypeAlias, 1765-1769 extendeeType), (2) when notOnStack returns false (5272-5281; count at its callers 3979, 4135/4142/4149 if it must stay non-mutating), (3) when the declarationsOnStack check at 4680 excludes an extension, and (4) at any other place where membership in declarationsOnStack changes a computed value rather than only a memo write. Grep `declarationsOnStack` and list every use in the PR.
Key: `struct MemberKey: Hashable { n: Name; q: AnyTypeIdentity; scope: ScopeIdentity }`, where scope = lookupScope(scopeOfUse). lookupScope is memoized: the nearest ancestor-or-self s with givens(lexicallyIn: s) non-empty, or a local ExtensionDeclaration or TraitDeclaration lexically in s, or else the file scope. Before using it, audit every use of scopeOfUse in the call tree of resolve(_:memberOf:visibleFrom:) (4590-4609): nativeMemberOf 4635-4657, memberInExtensionOf 4665-4671, declaredIn 4675-4708, applies 4944-4973 (normalized by givens), inheritedMemberOf 4715-4745 (summon, normalized by givens), traits/extensions(visibleFrom:) 4903-4939 and 5035-5061. Confirm that each depends on scopeOfUse only through the things lookupScope preserves. If anything else depends on it (accessibility, for instance), add it to the key or use the raw file + lookupScope pair.
In resolve(_:memberOf:visibleFrom:): Namespace qualifications go to a separate `builtinMemo[Name]` for `.builtin`, if resolve(builtin:) is verified pure. When the flag is on, `!q[.hasVariable]` and `declarationsOnStack.isEmpty`: on a hit, return the entry. On a miss, record `let c0 = stackObservations`, compute as today, and store only if `stackObservations == c0` and no candidate.type has .hasVariable.
Counters: membermemo.hit, miss, tainted, varResult.
Verify mode: HYLO_TC_MEMBERMEMO_VERIFY=1 recomputes on every hit and asserts that the candidates are equal (reference and type). Use it for the gate runs.
Soundness (strict): the writer runs with an empty stack. Every sub-result it used was (i) read from a write-once memo or program table, (ii) computed and memoized during the call, or (iii) computed without memoizing. With no stack observation during the call, nothing in (ii) or (iii) depended on stack contents, and no cycle cut fed a transient .error into the result. A baseline recomputation at a later empty-stack reader is deterministic. It reads the same write-once values that the writer read or wrote, so it produces the same candidates. The skipped recomputation has no observable effect: its sub-results are memoized or recomputed identically, and resolve(memberOf:) reports no diagnostics itself, since diagnostics from first-time typing happen in the writer exactly as in the baseline. The other flags (index, absmodel, givenfacts) take the same path at an empty stack, so the memo replays the configured pipeline, which keeps it independent of other flags. Remaining residual: fresh-variable numbering.
Test: semtest with membermemo alone and with all flags, run in verify mode, on the corpus, the stdlib, the workloads and review/names/*.hylo. Measure membermemo.hit on the stdlib; about 800-1000 hits are expected, given that about 8.2% of memberOf calls come from declaredType with a non-empty stack.
slate.expected_gain: stdlib about -5 to -8% of typing on its own (strict mode); about -3 to -5% on top of nocopy, givenfacts and memberskip. members-big: half of its 2000 lookups repeat (about 1100 distinct), so about -20% without memberskip and -2% with it. breadth80, ovl and ovr only through the stdlib.

Index's coercionSources becomes unnecessary; its summon bucket is still needed (and dtree would supersede it).

H6 (unify vs typevec): unify changes no counter, so its value is constant-factor only. Hypothesis: once typevec's tag-first cast and alias-probe skip land, unify's remaining gain (sequential cast chain in unifiableSameShape) falls below about 1%. ideas.name: typevec
ideas.summary: Give TypeStore its own in-module storage when the flag is on: a ContiguousArray<AnyTypeTree> `trees` (indexed by identity offset), a parallel [UInt8] `tags` (TypeTag index), and a specialized Swift Dictionary<AnyTypeTree, Int> for interning. This replaces StableSet<AnyTypeTree>. StableSet/StableDictionary live in another module and are neither @inlinable nor specialized, so each type projection runs unspecialized generic code: it builds the (key, value) tuple through swift_getTupleTypeMetadata2 (called twice), instantiates Bucket and StableSet.Empty metadata, retains and releases the buffer, and copies key and value through value witnesses. Once the tags array exists, tag(of:), cast(_:to:), castUnchecked, isParameter, hasContext, head, contextAndHead and open check the tag first and do not copy the existential at all in the common case (a type with no context).

ideas.expected_gain: stdlib typing: about -12 to -16%, i.e. 20-25 ms of about 160 ms (StableSet.subscript goes from 12.6% to roughly 1.5-2% for the array index plus existential copy; interning loses about 2% of generic overhead; contextAndHead/head stop copying existentials for context-free types). breadth80: about -15 to -20% of the whole run (25.8% of samples sit in these two entry points). members-big: about -4%. ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10: the same share as stdlib (their user part is small). After symindex removes 13.7%, the relative share grows to about 15-18%.
ideas.soundness: Exact. The TypeStore storage is private, and the only mutation is insert(_:) (TypeStore.swift:93), so the StableSet never removes anything. In StableDictionary.lookup a not-found key returns `emptyBucket == -1 ? end : emptyBucket`. emptyBucket is set only for tombstones (truncatedHash 0x7f), which only remove(at:) writes, and insert at p == end sets end = p + 1. The position of a new tree is therefore always the current count, which is exactly trees.count before the append. An existing tree is found by the same Hashable/Equatable relation (AnyTypeTree's hash(into:) and ==), so it gets the same offset. Every AnyTypeIdentity therefore has bit-identical offsets and properties, and all downstream behaviour (orderings, memo keys, elaboration, diagnostics) is unchanged. Hash seeds do not matter because positions come from insertion order. tags[i] is written once, at insertion, from type(of: t), so `tag(of:)` gives the same answer as `.init(type(of: self[n]))`. head and contextAndHead only skip the projection when the tag is neither UniversalType nor Implication, which is exactly the `default:` branch.
ideas.overlaps_with: Orthogonal to all six flags and to dtree, symindex, memberindex and probereuse. It speeds up everything that projects types: canDeriveCoercions (dtree's target), unify's tag dispatch, solver propagation. It makes `unify` slightly cheaper still, but `unify` stays useful because it removes the sequential cast chain. No existing flag becomes unnecessary. It composes with internfast and tagswitch below, which get larger wins from the `tags` array.
ideas.implementation_sketch: In TypeStore add `private let fast = TyperExperiments.typevec`, `private var trees: ContiguousArray<AnyTypeTree> = []`, `private var tags: [UInt8] = []` and `private var index: [AnyTypeTree: Int] = [:]`. In insert: `if fast { let k = AnyTypeTree(t); if let i = index[k] { return .init(offset: i, properties: t.properties) }; let i = trees.count; index[k] = i; trees.append(k); tags.append(UInt8(TypeTag.indices[TypeTag(type(of: t))]!)); return .init(offset: i, properties: t.properties) }`. Better: one `index[k, default: trees.count]` probe via a modify accessor. In subscript(AnyTypeIdentity), in the default branch: `fast ? trees[n.offset].wrapped : types[n.offset].wrapped`. Add `func tagIndex(_ n: AnyTypeIdentity) -> UInt8?` that returns nil for predefined identities and variables and tags[n.offset] otherwise, with static constants for UniversalType, Implication, TypeAlias and so on. In cast(_:to:): `if fast, let k = tagIndex(n) { return k == U.tagIndex ? .init(uncheckedFrom: n.erased) : nil }`. In head/contextAndHead/open: `if fast, let k = tagIndex(h), k != uni, k != impl { return ... }` before the `switch self[h]`. count and reserveCapacity forward to trees and index when fast. Gate by running semtest on the whole corpus with each other flag combination.

ideas.name: internfast
ideas.summary: Remove the runtime casts and the generic-metadata work from interning. (a) demand<T: TypeTree>(_:) tests T.self == ErrorType.self, Tuple.self, UniversalType.self and TypeVariable.self, which fold at compile time in each specialization. demand(any:) compares type(of: t) with those metatypes (pointer compares) and calls `as!` only on the one branch that matched. Today every demand, even in specializations for Arrow, TypeWitness or MachineType, makes 4 swift_dynamicCast calls and also boxes the value into an existential (swift_allocObject for large trees). (b) TypeTree.equals(_:) is rewritten from `self == other as? Self` to `guard type(of: other) == Self.self, let o = other as? Self else { return false }; return self == o`. The current form compiles to an unspecialized Optional<Self> == Optional<Self>, which instantiates Optional metadata and calls swift_getTupleTypeMetadata2 for the (Self?, Self?) switch on every key comparison during interning.

New flag in TyperExperiments, read once (e.g. a TypeStore stored let, or a `static let`).

TypeTree.equals 2.81% inclusive, of which __swift_instantiateCanonicalPrespecializedGenericMetadata is 0.69%, swift_getTupleTypeMetadata2 0.69% and swift_dynamicCast 0.29%. The cast/conformance attribution (attr-typing-d1.txt) puts demand(any:) at 1.51% of typing. breadth80 (attr-stress.txt): TypeTree.equals under StableDictionary.lookup has generic metadata 1.48%, retain/release 0.71%, casts 0.47% and tuple metadata; demand(any:) casts 0.47%. Disassembly (disasm-evidence.txt): `specialized TypeStore.demand(any:)` for Arrow calls swift_allocObject and then swift_dynamicCast 4 times; TypeTree.equals calls the Optional metadata accessor and getTupleTypeMetadata2 before swift_dynamicCast.

ideas.soundness: Exact. Every TypeTree conformer is a struct or enum, so there are no subclasses and `x is S` on an existential holds iff type(of: x) == S.self. In demand<T>, T is always a concrete conformer: `any TypeTree` cannot satisfy T: TypeTree because TypeTree refines Hashable. So the static comparisons pick the same branch as the dynamic `switch`. The `where` guards (u == .empty, isNever(u)) run unchanged on the cast value. For equals: if the dynamic types differ, `other as? Self` is nil and the old code compares the non-nil self with nil, which is false, the same as the early return. Otherwise `as? Self` succeeds and both forms evaluate `self == o`. The returned identities are identical.
ideas.overlaps_with: Independent of all six flags. Complements typevec: typevec removes the StableDictionary overhead around the comparisons, and this removes the overhead inside them. Both can sit under one flag if you prefer fewer flags. No overlap with dtree, symindex or memberindex.

Tuple) == .empty { return .init(uncheckedFrom: .void) }; if T.self == UniversalType.self, isNever(t as! UniversalType) { ... .never }; if T.self == TypeVariable.self { return .init(uncheckedFrom: AnyTypeIdentity(variable: (t as! TypeVariable).identifier)) }; return .init(uncheckedFrom: insert(t)) }`. Make insert generic (`insert<U: TypeTree>(_ t: U)`) so that boxing happens once, into AnyTypeTree. demand(any:): `let m = type(of: t); if m == ErrorType.self {...} else if m == Tuple.self, ...`. TypeTree.equals: the guard form above, chosen by the flag (one flag read per comparison; cache it in a `static let`).

ideas.name: nocopy
ideas.summary: Remove whole-Typer and whole-Program copies that come from method partial applications and from an escaping AnyIterator. Swift evaluates `xs.filter(resolvableWithQualification(_:))` inside a mutating method of a struct by copying `self` into a context (one value-witness copy and one destroy of Typer, i.e. Program plus about 22 memo dictionaries, each retained and released). `allSatisfy(program.isOverloadable(_:))` and `contains(where: program.isImplicit)` copy Program. Program.scopes(from:) returns `some Sequence` backed by AnyIterator { ... }, which allocates three heap objects and copies Program into an escaping closure on every call. The fix replaces each with a non-escaping closure literal (`{ resolvableWithQualification($0) }`, which captures self by address), skips the filter entirely when the lookup result is empty, and walks scopes with a plain `var s: ScopeIdentity? = x; while let t = s { ...; s = program.parent(containing: t) }` loop at the Typer call sites.

Disassembly (disasm-evidence.txt): the loop body of lookup(memberOfTraitVisibleFrom:) calls 'outlined init with copy of Typer' and later 'outlined destroy of Typer'; Program.scopes(from:) makes 3 swift_allocObject calls plus 'outlined init with copy of Program'; hasImplicitOnStack copies Program twice.

ideas.soundness: Exact. The same predicate is applied to the same elements in the same order. Only the capture mode changes: a non-escaping closure literal borrows self (or inout self) instead of snapshotting it, and the predicates are pure reads, so the snapshot and the live value agree while filter runs (nothing mutates self during the call). Skipping filter on an empty array returns the same empty array. The manual scope loop visits exactly the sequence s, parent(s), ... until node == nil, as the AnyIterator does.

With nocopy on, memberindex's stdlib gain drops to about 1-2%, but its members-big gain (extension side) is unchanged. Independent of the six existing flags.

ideas.name: tagswitch
ideas.summary: Dispatch on cheap tags or property bits before projecting and casting in the hottest `switch self[x] { case let t as A: ... case let t as B: ... }` chains of TypeStore and Typer. ideas.soundness: Exact up to fresh-variable numbering and type-store insertion order, which index and names already perturb. (1) Purity of the inputs. Through Name, q and the scope, the result depends only on: declarations(nativeMembersOf:) and declarations(lexicallyIn:) (syntactic and memoized); extensions(visibleFrom:) and traits(visibleFrom:), which are fixed per lookup-scope by construction of the normalization (the nearest ancestor with lexical givens, extensions or traits, or the file; files differ by imports); summon and applies, which already normalize by givens and are memoized when the type is closed and no implicit is on the stack; and declaredType and typeOfImplementation of members, which are memoized permanently in the program (setType) after the first computation. Candidate witnesses are reified with .substitutedByError, so the fresh trait-parameter variables never appear in the result. (2) Validity (relaxed mode). Write an entry only when q is closed (no .hasVariable), no implicit or extension declaration is on the stack at entry, and `cycleCuts` did not change during the call. The counter is bumped at every stack observation that can change an outcome: the four cycle branches, notOnStack returning false, and the extension filter at 4681. Read an entry only when no implicit or extension declaration is on the stack. Argument: a later baseline recomputation could differ only if (a) it observes the stack, or (b) a memo or program entry it reads changed. For (a): implicit and extension entries are excluded at read time, and any other declaration x on the reader's stack has an unmemoized type. The writer needed declaredType(x) only if it computed it, which memoizes it, or hit a cycle on it, which taints the write. So the recomputation cannot hit x. For (b): program types and Memos entries are write-once. Every sub-query the writer computed without memoizing is recomputed deterministically from entries that were already fixed when the writer ran. Poisoned (cycle-cut) values can only enter on the first computation of a declaration's type, and every such first computation the writer depended on already happened during the writer's call, and cleanly, otherwise the counter would have moved. (3) The memo never changes which diagnostics are reported: resolve(memberOf:) reports nothing itself, and the nested first-time typings run in the writer exactly as in the baseline. (4) Independence from other flags: the memo replays whatever the configured pipeline computed. With index or absmodel on, the writer may have taken the unindexed path (non-empty stack) where a later baseline call would take the indexed one. That is equal if index is sound. For strict independence, offer strict mode: write and read only when the stack is empty. The L1 memos (trait members per (Name, lookup-scope), Builtin per Name) are purely syntactic and always valid. resolvableWithQualification and refineLookupResults depend only on syntax.
ideas.overlaps_with: memberindex: both remove the per-call trait scan. memberindex also speeds up first-time lookups (members-big); membermemo also removes nativeMemberOf, qualificationForSelection, reify and typeOfImplementation on repeats. They are complementary, and with membermemo on, memberindex is needed only for workloads with many distinct (name, type) pairs. names: membermemo makes names irrelevant for repeated lookups but not for first-time ones (members-big). The `cycleCuts` taint counter is the same infrastructure the names review asks for (names-1 suggested fix (1)), so it can be shared with `cyclecut`. Independent of unify, solver (it also removes the re-resolution of a member in each solver fork and probe), loopcheck, index and absmodel (see the strict-mode caveat).

ideas.soundness: Let `settled(g)` mean: .user(d) or .nested(_, .user(d)) with program[d.module].type(assignedTo: d) != nil, or g is .coercion, .recursive or .assumed. Once settled, declaredType(g) is a fixed value: setType is write-once, and for .nested, contextOfSelf goes through the typeOfTraitSelf memo and introduce is hash-consed, so demand returns the already-interned id with no new insertion. canDeriveCoercion(p, g) for a settled g is a pure function of that type and p, except that its equality branch calls open(), which only allocates fresh variables. Hence: (a) skipping a settled non-source returns 0b00 exactly as the baseline does, and the skipped declaredType call has no effect; (b) writing the (g, p) memo for closed p under an implicit stack stores the value every later computation would produce, and the baseline already reads that memo under any stack; (c) unsettled givens fall back to the baseline path, which also fills the facts, so evaluation order and cycle side effects are unchanged. For the aggregate canDeriveCoercions, the visible list is cached unfiltered per scope (it depends only on syntax and memoized imports) and filtered by notOnStack only when an implicit is on the stack, which reproduces 4135-4149 exactly, including the order. Extra aggregate entries computed under a stack go to a separate table. That table is read only when the reader's on-stack implicit declarations contain no coercion source, because the baseline reads its own table unconditionally and must not see values it would not have written. The only perturbation is fresh-variable numbering in skipped equality-branch opens.

It reads declarations(lexicallyIn:) (memoized, fixed after scoping), program.isOverloadable, refineLookupResults (syntactic) and imports(of:). imports(of:) evaluates declaredType of import declarations once and memoizes it, so after the first call the result is a fixed function of (Name, scope). The memo for scope s stores the pair (accumulated result, shadowed flag) produced by the walk from s upward, and the entry for s is computed as append(local(s)) composed with the parent's entry. The outer part per (file, identifier) is the baseline loop over the other files (stopping at the first shadowing file) followed by the imports. It does not depend on the scope of use. ideas.name: cyclecut
ideas.summary: SEMANTIC CHANGE (baseline fix, keep separate). Do not memoize anything whose computation crossed a cycle cut. A counter `cycleCuts` is incremented in every 'refers to itself' branch. declaredType, extendeeType, summon, applies, canDeriveCoercion(s) and the given index record the counter at entry. They write their memo, or call setType, only if the counter did not move, so a value computed under a cut is recomputed in a clean context later. This removes order-dependent memoization, which is the root cause of the names unsoundness, and makes every caching or skipping flag order-independent. It also replaces the coarse hasImplicitOnStack() gates with a precise rule: memoize when the counter did not move, and key or scope the entry by the visible on-stack implicits. That rule allows memo writes during conformance checking.

ideas.name: solver1
ideas.summary: Make `solver` defer and probe only when two or more overload constraints are pending at the same time. A system with at most one pending overload set takes the baseline path: the overload is solved as soon as it is popped, by forking every candidate, with no probe and no commit. This removes the cost `solver` adds on the stdlib, where it prunes nothing, and makes single-overload systems identical to the baseline, which removes the known overload-priority.hylo divergence. The multi-overload wins (ovl, ovr) are kept.
ideas.code_locations: Solver.swift:102 (let deferring = TyperExperiments.solver): make deferring dynamic (solver1 && pendingOverloads >= 2). Solver.swift:147-151 (the `case is OverloadConstraint` park branch): park only when another OverloadConstraint is already in fresh or parked; otherwise call me.solve(overload: g) as the baseline does. Solver.swift:105-118 (loop-top handling of parked goals and the refresh) and :166 (`if fresh.isEmpty && !deferring`): test parked.isEmpty instead of !deferring, so that the refresh timing equals the baseline whenever nothing is parked. Solver.swift:594-630 resolveParked: when parked.count == 1, call solve(overload:among: k.candidates) without probing. Add a counter pendingOverloads that insert(fresh:) (Solver.swift:796) increments for each OverloadConstraint and that is decremented when an overload is solved or committed.
ideas.expected_gain: Stdlib: about -3 to -6% of typing. Most of the 338 probes go (about 300 or more), goalSteps returns to about 9.5k, and the parked-related refresh scans disappear. This is consistent with the noisy -7 to -15% for all-minus-solver. ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10: unchanged, still about 4 orders of magnitude better than the baseline. The final parked set is forked instead of committed, which costs a few forks. breadth80, members-big and chain: no change.
ideas.soundness: In a system where two overload constraints are never pending at the same time, the solver never parks. The run then executes exactly the baseline statements: overloads are solved when popped, and refreshCoercionAndWideningConstraints runs whenever fresh empties after a running step. Loop-top refresh plus break is equivalent to line 166 plus the while condition, so for those systems the result is identical by construction. Overloads created later inside forks are handled by the fork with the same rule. For systems with two or more simultaneous overloads, the flag behaves like the current solver. It inherits whatever argument solver has there; the unfinished solver review and the known commit-path representation issue (X vs A<Void>) still apply. So solver1 strictly shrinks solver's divergence surface; it does not prove it empty. The commit path should additionally be fixed to record the choice the same way solve(overload:) does.
ideas.overlaps_with: Replaces `solver`; with solver1 available, `solver` is unnecessary. Complementary to probereuse (ideas/RESULTS-partial.md), which makes the remaining probes cheaper. Independent of names, unify, index, absmodel and loopcheck: counters show no interaction (solver changes no summon counters except about 87 summon calls served by cache hits).
ideas.implementation_sketch: In Solver: `private var pendingOverloads = 0`. In insert(fresh:), `if k is OverloadConstraint { pendingOverloads += 1 }`, and copy it in forking init. In the OverloadConstraint case: `if TyperExperiments.solver1 && (pendingOverloads >= 2 || !me.parked.isEmpty) { me.parked.append(g); return .running }`; otherwise `me.pendingOverloads -= 1; return me.solve(overload: g)...` (the same as the baseline). In resolveParked, decrement for the removed goal, and `if parked.isEmpty && fresh-has-no-overload { return solve(overload: g, among: k.candidates) }` without probing. Replace `!deferring` at line 166 with `parked.isEmpty`. Gate: semtest on the 192 tests (overload-priority.hylo must become identical) plus the ovl/ovr workloads (counters probes/commits must remain).

ideas.name: abslite
ideas.summary: Remove absmodel's build overhead without changing any refutation. (a) Default HYLO_TC_ABSDEPTH to 2 instead of 3: k=3 makes stdlib typing about 18x slower and refutes nothing more. (b) In AbstractResolutionModel.insert, keep a hash set of the ground, top-free facts for each key next to the ordered bucket, and append in place. Today each insert copies the bucket array (copy-on-write while the dictionary still holds it) and runs a linear subsumption scan, which is quadratic per key. (c) In mayDerive, check the set first for a ground, top-free query, and pre-offset non-ground facts once at insertion instead of allocating renamed copies on every query.
ideas.code_locations: TyperCounters.swift:65-68 (absDepth default 3 -> 2). AbstractResolution.swift:223-231 insert (`var bucket = facts[k] ?? []`, the linear `bucket.contains(where: subsumes)`, `facts[k] = bucket`). AbstractResolution.swift:117-127 mayDerive (`f.offsettingVariables(by: 1 << 20)` for every non-ground fact on every query). Add `exact: [Key: Set<Term>]` and `general: [Key: [Term]]` (facts that contain variables or .top) next to `facts`. Typer.swift:3979-3990 abstractModel (unchanged; only the model internals change).
ideas.profile_evidence: absDepth hazard, measured today on bin 4587ce9e1a23 with index,absmodel on the stdlib: no HYLO_TC_ABSDEPTH gives absmodel.work=3,768,008, facts=14082, micros=14.0 s, type.stdlib 14876 ms, refuted=224. k=2 gives work=14783, facts=1399, micros=12.5 ms, type.stdlib 796 ms, refuted=225. breadth80 (all on): absmodel.built=1, facts=6463, work=654 (saturation is trivial), absmodel.refuted=0, absmodel.micros=35-53 ms of about 350-430 ms user typing (10-15%). breadth80 has 80 keys x 80 ground facts. The insert scans give 80*79/2*80, about 253k subsumes() calls, each allocating a dictionary and a closure box, plus about 6400 bucket copies of up to 80 elements. Leave-one-out confirms the flag is pure cost there: all minus absmodel gives identical summon counters. On the stdlib, micros is 12-25 ms (1.5-2.5% of a loaded run). That figure also includes the declaredType forcing that the index would otherwise do.
ideas.expected_gain: breadth80 user typing: about -8 to -12% (the 35-50 ms absmodel.micros drops to a few ms). Stdlib: about -0.5 to -1.5%. div-*, chain, ovl and ovr: model builds of 63-65 facts, so negligible. (a) alone removes a 14-18x stdlib slowdown for anyone who runs absmodel without the environment variable.
ideas.soundness: (a) Any depth k gives a sound over-approximation, so k=2 refutes only failing subgoals, and the elaboration is identical (the depth only changes which failing threads are cut early). (b) For a ground, top-free f, subsumes(g, f) is true iff g == f when g is ground and top-free; otherwise it requires the full check. So `exact.contains(f) || general[k].contains(where: { subsumes($0, f) })` returns exactly what the current linear scan returns. The insert decisions, factCount, bucket order (still appended to the array in the same order) and therefore isInconclusive and the factLimit behaviour are all unchanged. (c) For a ground, top-free query q, unify(q, f) with ground, top-free f is q == f. Other facts are still scanned in order. Pre-offsetting by the same constant 1<<20 yields identical terms. mayDerive therefore returns the same Bool for every query, so the refutation set is bit-identical to today's absmodel.
ideas.overlaps_with: A refinement of `absmodel`, and only useful with it (or with any future absindex or dtree companion that queries the model). It does not overlap with the other flags. Redundancy finding: absmodel is NOT redundant with index. On the stdlib, with all other flags on, absmodel still removes 36/327 subgoals, 516/4057 matches and 114/341 layers. div-grow-20 needs it (210 subgoals and 400 matches with index alone, 21 and 20 with it). members-big, ovl and ovr reach the same counters with either index or absmodel. breadth80 and chain gain nothing from it.
ideas.implementation_sketch: Add the flag `abslite` and read it in AbstractResolutionModel.init (store a Bool). In insert: `if abslite { let gnd = f.isGroundTopFree; if gnd && exact[k, default: []].contains(f) { return false }; if general[k]?.contains(where: { Self.subsumes($0, f) }) == true { return false }; if !gnd, (facts[k] ?? []).contains(where: { Self.subsumes($0, f) }) { return false }; facts[k, default: []].append(f); if gnd { exact[k, default: []].insert(f) } else { general[k, default: []].append(f); offset[k, default: []].append(f.offsettingVariables(by: 1 << 20)) }; factCount += 1; return true }`. (A non-ground f can be subsumed by a ground fact only through .top or equality, so that case keeps the full scan.) In mayDerive: `if q.isGroundTopFree { if exact[k]?.contains(q) == true { return true }; scan only general/offset[k] }`; otherwise scan as today, using the pre-offset copies. Separately, change the absDepth default to 2. Validate that all absmodel.* counters (refuted, facts, inconclusive) are identical to absmodel without abslite on every workload.

ideas.name: loopsafe
ideas.summary: Replace the unsound `loopcheck` with a sound restriction. A subgoal identical to an ancestor is pruned only when (1) it has no unification variables, and (2) the stack of pending assumed givens is the same as at that ancestor, i.e. environment.givens.count is equal. Each ancestor is stored once, reified when it is pushed, with its pending-givens count, so the per-subgoal ancestor re-reification goes away. loopcheck's measured counterexamples all reuse a pending premise of an intermediate implication (shared lemma), which condition (2) excludes.
ideas.code_locations: Typer.swift:3640-3650 (the loopcheck block in summon(_:in:where:then:penalties:ancestors:) reifies t and every ancestor on every call). Typer.swift:3719-3723 formThread (`e.ancestry[...] = ancestors.appending(queried)`). Typer.swift:3514 Environment.ancestry: [Int: [AnyTypeIdentity]], which would become [Int: [(type: AnyTypeIdentity, pending: Int)]]. Typer.swift:3794-3805 threadContinuation (the ancestry hand-off). The ancestors parameter type changes accordingly.
ideas.profile_evidence: Leave-one-out counters (research/ideas/redundancy/loo-tables.txt): loopcheck.pruned is 0, and all counters are identical to all-on, on the stdlib, breadth80, chain8/9, div-dead/grow/loop-20, members-big, ovl-8-8 and ovr-3-10. With absmodel on, loopcheck removes no work on any workload. It acts only when absmodel is off (div-dead-20 and div-loop-20: pruned=21). Soundness, re-run today on bin 4587ce9e1a23 (research/ideas/redundancy/lc/, dumps normalized as in tcx.py): lc04, lc05, lc06, lc07 and lc12 differ from the baseline both with loopcheck alone and with all six flags. All flags minus loopcheck is identical to the baseline on every one of them, so absmodel does not mask the bug (loopcheck.pruned=1-2 there). Niche value: on lc08 the baseline aborts (out of memory at the 2.5 GB cap) while loopcheck terminates with a diagnostic; on lc14 the baseline produces no output while loopcheck terminates. Under all minus loopcheck, lc14 aborts out of memory and lc08 produces no output, so absmodel cannot stop these loops (generic self-loops).
ideas.expected_gain: Speed: about 0% on the stdlib and the stress workloads (nothing is pruned there). The ancestor bookkeeping drops from O(depth) reifies per subgoal to O(depth) identity compares, or O(1) with a set. The value is soundness: the default flag set gets a loop-pruner that matches the baseline on lc01-lc15. It also keeps the termination win on single-premise self-loops (div-loop without absmodel, lc08 rules 1 and 3).
ideas.soundness: Suppose s == a after reification, s is ground, and the pending-givens stack at s equals the one at a. Because environment.givens is a stack, equal counts inside a's subtree mean an identical stack. Then the candidate set at s (assumed givens, visible givens, built-ins, all in the same scope) and the candidate penalty offsets equal those at a, so every derivation D of s is also available as a thread at a. That thread takes strictly fewer BFS steps (at least the match that led from a to s is skipped), and its penalty is no larger (penalties never decrease along a thread). Because a is ground, a's subtree cannot bind variables outside it, so a's continuation is identical. takeSummonResults stops at the first layer that has a done thread, and the alternative finishes strictly earlier, so the pruned thread can never be among the returned results, and the depth cap reaches the alternative first. loopcheck's counterexamples break condition (2): the inner `SA is T` sees the pending `SP is T` of g1 and is pruned by loopcheck, but loopsafe does not prune it. Caveat: the argument assumes that canDeriveCoercions and the index or absmodel decisions depend only on (type, scope, environment.givens), which holds today. Gate it with semtest on review/loopcheck/lc01-lc15 plus the corpus. lc14 (a two-premise self-loop with a pending identical sibling) is not pruned by loopsafe, so it still exhausts memory like the baseline.
ideas.overlaps_with: Replaces `loopcheck`, which should be dropped from the recommended set: it is redundant with absmodel on every measured workload and unsound on 5 review programs. Partly overlaps with absmodel on divergence (div-dead and div-loop are handled by both, div-grow only by absmodel, generic self-loops like lc08 only by loopsafe or loopcheck). Subsumed by knuthtable if that semantic change is ever adopted.
ideas.implementation_sketch: In formThread (Typer.swift:3719), under loopsafe: `if !queried[.hasVariable] { e.ancestry[id] = ancestors + [(queried, environment.givens.count)] } else { e.ancestry[id] = ancestors }`. The queried type is already reified there; ground types do not change under later substitutions, so no re-reify is needed. In summon(where:) (3640): `if loopsafe, !ancestors.isEmpty { let u = reify(t, ...); if !u[.hasVariable], ancestors.contains(where: { $0.type == u && $0.pending == environment.givens.count }) { bump(loopsafe.pruned); return [] } }`. Optional: keep a parallel Set<AnyTypeIdentity> for O(1) membership.

ideas.name: absseed
ideas.summary: Seed the abstract model of an importing module from the already-saturated model of the module it imports (in practice the stdlib's top-level model), and then add only the module's own givens with the existing incremental saturate(from:). Today the first query in each user module rebuilds the model from scratch over all visible givens, including every stdlib given. That fixed cost is about 1.4-2.2 ms per module and dominates the user typing of small programs.
ideas.code_locations: Typer.swift:3965-3990 abstractModel(visibleFrom:): the `else` branch (`m = AbstractResolutionModel(depth:); local = Array(givens(visibleFrom: scopeOfUse).joined())`) taken for the first file scope of a module. Typer.swift:4130-4154 givens(visibleFrom:) (the imported group is givens(atTopLevelOf: i)). The cache moduleToAbstractModel is in Memos (Typer.swift:76-85).
ideas.profile_evidence: absmodel.micros for the user module with all flags on (c2): chain8 1393 us of 2.64 ms user typing (about 50%), ovl-8-8 2241 us of 10.9 ms (about 20%), members-big 2250 us (0.2%), div-* about 1-2 ms. In all of them absmodel.facts=63-65 and work=654-656: the same model, rebuilt from the stdlib's givens for each module. The stdlib's own top-level model (built while typing the stdlib, about 1399 facts over 22 builds) is already in cache.moduleToAbstractModel[stdlib].
ideas.expected_gain: User typing: about -1.5 to -2 ms per module (chain8 -50%, ovl-8-8 -15 to -20%, div-* -20 to -40%). Stdlib: 0. Every real compilation saves this once per module whenever absmodel is on.
ideas.soundness: The least model of truncated Horn clauses is the unique least fixpoint, whatever order the clauses are added in. Starting from the imported module's saturated model, with the module's own clauses added and saturate(from: firstNew) run, gives a fact set with the same denotation as a from-scratch build. abstractModel(visibleFrom:) for nested scopes already relies on this monotonicity. mayDerive(q) is true iff some fact has an instance in common with q, which depends only on the denotation. The representation (subsumption order, factCount) may differ, and so may whether factLimit is reached. Inconclusive only means no refutation is made, and every refutation is of a failing subgoal (assuming absmodel is sound), so the elaboration is unchanged either way. Requirement: the imported model must have been built from exactly givens(atTopLevelOf: imported module). It is built when declarationsOnStack is empty, so notOnStack excluded nothing. Check this with a debug assertion comparing clause counts. With several imports, start from one module's model and add the other modules' clauses.
ideas.overlaps_with: A refinement of `absmodel`; it does nothing without it. It composes with abslite (which makes each build cheaper) and does not overlap with the other flags.
ideas.implementation_sketch: In abstractModel(visibleFrom:), in the from-scratch branch under absseed: `let imps = imports(of: scopeOfUse.file); if let base = imps.first.flatMap({ cache.moduleToAbstractModel[$0] }), base.depth == TyperExperiments.absDepth { m = base; local = (local givens of this file's scopes, other files of the module, imports other than imps.first).filter(notOnStack) } else { as today }`. When a module is fully typed, also record its top-level model under moduleToAbstractModel (this already happens when the parent is nil). Validate that absmodel.refuted is identical with and without absseed on all workloads and the corpus, and that the semtest dump is identical.
